ar.why: L1 raised to infobox 410m (ours 270 is 34% below infobox, outside tolerance); added Chad (TCD), official Arabic co-official with French per constitution, matches '24 states' infobox count (ours only had 23).

aa.unsure: Wiktionary gives 'gadda ge' for thank-you vs ours 'Yakke'en'; no second source (no Wikivoyage) to confirm either, left unchanged.

ff.unsure: hello 'Jam na?' vs Wiktionary 'mihofnima' for Fula - both plausible Pulaar-region greetings, no Wikivoyage line to confirm either way, left unchanged.
ff.why: L1 raised to infobox 36.85m->37 (ours 24 matches a stale 2007 Wikidata figure, infobox 2014-2021 data is more current and used as main reference).

ak.why: 'Akwaaba' means 'welcome' (said by a host to a guest), not a general-purpose hello; Wiktionary gives time-of-day greetings maakye/maaha/maadwo, used morning/afternoon/evening as the actual everyday greeting.

kr.unsure: 'Yerima' for goodbye looks suspicious (it's a known Kanuri/Hausa title meaning 'crown prince'), but no Wikivoyage/Wiktionary goodbye line exists to confirm a replacement.
kr.why: ours (6/6) far below infobox 10.6m and Wikidata 15m; set L1 to infobox 2sf (11), total to Wikidata's broader figure (15); thanks replaced with Wikivoyage's phrasebook line which differs completely from ours.

lg.why: ours L1=11 actually matches the infobox TOTAL (L1 5.6m + L2 5.4m ~ 11m); corrected L1 to infobox's 5.6m, kept total=11 (already right). 'Kodi' is not a greeting (it means something like 'is anyone there?/excuse me'); Wikivoyage's actual hello is 'Oli otya' (to one person).

st.why: Added Zimbabwe: both Wikidata and the infobox nation field list it as an official/national language alongside South Africa and Lesotho.

ts.why: Added Zimbabwe (Shangani/Tsonga is one of Zimbabwe's 16 constitutionally recognized languages, confirmed by Wikidata+infobox). Thanks changed to Wikivoyage's phrasebook choice 'Inkomu' (ours 'Ndzi khense' is a more formal variant, Wikivoyage preferred for travellers).

umb.unsure: hello 'Kalunga' is suspicious - that word usually denotes a supreme deity/spirit in Umbundu-derived religions (Candomblé/Umbanda) rather than a greeting - but no Wiktionary/Wikivoyage data exists for Umbundu to confirm a replacement.
umb.why: Infobox nation field explicitly says Angola (national language status).

kri.why: ours l1=4m is ~5x the infobox (0.86m) and Wikidata (0.69m) figures; total raised to infobox total (L1 0.86m + L2 6.92m = 7.8m). Added Sierra Leone per Wikidata official_in. Hello diacritic corrected to match Wiktionary/Wikivoyage (Kushɛ). Goodbye 'A go so' replaced - both Wiktionary and Wikivoyage give 'a de go' for goodbye, a clear mismatch with ours.

wuu.why: Hello text '你好' is Mandarin, not Wu script - replaced with the Wu form '侬好' (儂好), matching Wiktionary/Wikivoyage. Thanks romanization 'Jiajia' did not match any source; Wikivoyage gives 'zhia6 zhia6' (Shanghai) for 謝謝, so rom/say updated to match.

ja.why: Added Palau: Japanese has official status on Angaur Island/Angaur State per Wikidata and the infobox nation field; kept Japan since it's near-universally cited as Japan's (de facto) official/national language in general references.

dz.why: ours l1=0.64m was actually the infobox's TOTAL figure (171,080 L1 / 640,000 total); L1 corrected to 0.17m, total (0.64) already right. Thanks script text was garbled; replaced with Wiktionary's བཀའ་དྲིན་ཆེ (rom/say already matched Wikivoyage's 'Kadrin chhe').

ps.why: Thanks script was missing a letter ('منه' -> 'مننه', matching Wiktionary's manana). Goodbye reworded to match Wikivoyage's actual phrasebook line 'په مخه مو ښه [pə məkha mo kha]' (ours had scrambled word order).

ku.why: Added Syria: infobox explicitly notes Kurdish is 'recognized as a national language' there. Goodbye script read like a Persian/Urdu 'khuda hafiz' borrowing that didn't match the rom/say fields at all; replaced with Kurdish script matching Wikivoyage's 'Bi xatirê te!' which the rom/say already reflected.

hy.why: ours l1=4m is 24% below the only infobox figure (5.28m combined Western+Eastern Armenian, no L1/L2 split given); raised to match since it's the best available current reference and total (5.5) was already close to it.

es.why: Added Western Sahara (Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic retains Spanish as an official language) - matches infobox's count of '21 countries, 1 territory, 1 partially recognized state' (ours only had 20 sovereign states).

ru.why: Added Tajikistan: both Wikidata and the infobox list it as an inter-ethnic language designated by the constitution, alongside the other co-official states.

be.why: ours l1=3.3m is below every reference (lowest is Wikidata's 5.058m, infobox gives 5.094m); raised to infobox's 2sf value.

sr.why: Removed Bosnia and Herzegovina: the infobox explicitly says Serbian is NOT official at the state level there, only within its sub-national entities (Federation of BiH / Republika Srpska) - regional-only per spec. Added Kosovo, where the infobox confirms Serbian is co-official nationally alongside Albanian. Montenegro not added: Serbian lost official status there in 2007 (now only a recognized minority 'language in official use').

sq.why: Added North Macedonia and Montenegro: both Wikidata and the infobox list Albanian as co-official there, alongside Albania and Kosovo.

gd.why: ours total=0.087m exceeded the infobox's defined L1+L2 Scotland figure (69,701) by ~25%; set to that reference. Goodbye 'Mar sin leat' matches none of Wiktionary's three options or Wikivoyage's 'Tioraidh!' - replaced with Wikivoyage's phrasebook choice.

ay.why: Removed Peru: the infobox's own footnote says Aymara is 'official only in Aymara-dominated areas' of Peru (a regional/local condition, not national-level per the spec's rule), unlike Bolivia where it is one of the 36 nationally official languages under the 2009 constitution.

quc.why: Spelling corrected from 'Maltyox' to 'Maltiox' to match Wiktionary.

fj.why: ours l1=0.64m actually matches the infobox TOTAL (L1 339,210 + L2 320,000 ~ 0.66m); L1 corrected to the infobox L1 figure (0.34m), total (0.64) already close to the implied total and left unchanged.
